comparison: Both strongly support the core geometrical readout mechanism (C2, C3, C39, C40, C41). OpenEval emphasizes extensive simulation validation across Figures 2-7, while peer reviewers praised it as a 'major contribution' and 'new benchmark.' Peer result R1 also includes C4 and C42 (model validation claims), which OpenEval addresses separately in R2. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with high confidence.

OpenEval R2 focuses on comprehensive validation (C4, C42, C43) showing the model outperforms existing models. Peer R1 includes C4 and C42 as part of the overall contribution. Both are SUPPORTED. The comparison with previous models (C43) is also addressed in peer R2, which specifically validates this comparative claim without challenge.

Both address the comparison with existing models. OpenEval R2 includes C43 (model outperforms previous models) as part of comprehensive validation. Peer R2 specifically validates the comparative claim (C25, C43) without challenge. Both are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R3 addresses protocol separation (C25-C28) with detailed simulations in Figure 2. Peer R2 validates C25 and C43 (comparative claims) without challenge. Both are SUPPORTED, though peer review focuses more narrowly on the comparison aspect while OpenEval includes mechanistic explanations (C26-C28).

Both address mechanistic explanations. OpenEval R3 includes C26-C28 (mechanistic differences between protocols) as part of protocol separation analysis. Peer R11 validates these same mechanistic explanations (C26, C27, C28, C60) and notes reviewers requested better explanation of nonlinear effects. Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect match on claims C72, C74, C77-C79 regarding age-dependent plasticity and BCM curve reproduction. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes Figure 4-5 validation and mechanistic dissection, while peer reviewers accepted results after clarification about free versus fixed parameters.

Perfect match on claims C80, C81, C86-C88, C90 regarding reproduction of Inglebert et al. 2020 data and sensitivity to extracellular conditions. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED without challenge. OpenEval emphasizes biophysical mechanisms incorporated, peer reviewers accepted as one of nine successfully reproduced experiments.

Perfect match on claims C5, C33, C34, C37, C38, C61 regarding noise effects and millisecond timescales. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C61 is more inference than direct validation, while peer reviewers specifically requested and accepted these predictions as valid model outputs, finding the nonlinear effects 'pretty cool.'

Perfect match on claims C29-C31 regarding nonlinear boundaries and differential timescales in the readout mechanism. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes experimental justification and Figure 3 supplement 3, while peer reviewers accepted these design features without challenge, requesting only better explanation of resulting nonlinear effects.

Strong overlap on stochasticity claims (C16, C17, C56, C57, C91, C93, C94). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on experimental citations and systematic analysis. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, extensively questioning noise implementation, critical noise sources, and deterministic SK channel modeling. This represents a significant disagreement - OpenEval found evidence sufficient while peer reviewers required additional clarification before acceptance.

Perfect match on model predictions (C58, C59, C75, C76, C89). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN because predictions extend beyond fitted data and lack experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting these as valid model outputs after authors provided additional predictions. This represents disagreement - peer reviewers were more accepting of untested predictions than OpenEval.

Strong overlap on temporal averaging and noise tolerance mechanisms (C47-C49). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as well-supported mechanistic insights. Peer R13 also rates SUPPORTED, accepting these interpretations about how the system achieves robust plasticity. Both agree these are valid conclusions from model analysis. OpenEval R10 also includes C60 which appears in peer R11.

Partial overlap on C60 (balance between attenuating and accumulating variables). OpenEval R10 includes this as part of mechanistic insights (SUPPORTED). Peer R11 includes C60 with mechanistic explanations C26-C28 (SUPPORTED). Both accept this as a key insight about the model's operation.

Strong overlap on model scope and limitations (C50-C54). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these as honest assessments of what the model captures. Peer reviewers accepted these as appropriate model features and acknowledged limitations without challenge. Peer R12 also includes C45 and C55 not in OpenEval R11.

OpenEval R12 addresses generalizability claims (C6, C62) and rates them UNCERTAIN as untested hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not specifically address the generalizability to other synapse types.

OpenEval R13 addresses background knowledge and literature review (C1, C7-C15), rating them SUPPORTED as well-cited established work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not specifically evaluate these background claims.

Peer R9 addresses presynaptic model claims (C63-C66, C82-C85) and rates them UNCERTAIN due to extensive criticism about phenomenological nature, too many parameters, and lack of biological interpretability. No corresponding OpenEval result found - OpenEval did not separately evaluate the presynaptic model components.

Peer R10 addresses temporal dynamics claims (C18-C24) and rates them SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the multi-timescale nature as a key feature. No corresponding OpenEval result found - OpenEval did not separately evaluate these temporal dynamics claims.

Peer R14 addresses experimental manipulation validation (C92) and rates it SUPPORTED without challenge. No corresponding OpenEval result found - OpenEval did not separately evaluate this specific validation claim.
